scenes.heading: Getting licensed and choosing a brokerage to start with

sents.d: Getting licensed and choosing a brokerage to start with
Licensing requirements and brokerage culture both vary significantly.

Licensing requirements — required coursework, exams, and ongoing continuing education — vary by region, so confirming the specific requirements where you plan to practice is the necessary first step before anything else.

New agents typically must work under a sponsoring brokerage, and brokerages vary widely in commission split, training and mentorship support, lead generation help, and monthly fees — all worth comparing rather than choosing based on brand recognition alone.

A brokerage with strong mentorship and training tends to matter more for a brand-new agent's first year than a slightly better commission split, since the split has little value if you're not closing deals yet.

take: Get licensed, then pick a brokerage for training over split.
